headNote: `head` names the commit this evidence pass ran at, and the stamps beside it describe that commit's trees - the pair `check-evidence.mjs` asserts against `HEAD:src`/`HEAD:scripts`. The commit this file rides in changes `docs/evidence` alone, so its two tree hashes are identical to `head`'s and the stamps hold across the pair. This is the REBASE ONTO `97467e5a9` (`main`, `package.json` `0.22.1`: the 0.22.0 and 0.22.1 releases, #167), which replayed this branch's fourteen commits onto a moved base and moved the merge-base with them, so every value here was re-derived rather than carried across: `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` from `git rev-parse HEAD:src`/`HEAD:scripts`, `surfaces`/`themes` from the capturer's own lists, `frames` from the frames on disk outside the declared sets. Two of those numbers moved for a reason that is not this branch's: `surfaces` 132 -> 161 and `frames` 1106 -> 1164, because `main` grew its `STORIES` list (123 entries at the old base, 152 now) and its evidence tree under this branch, so the honest value is counted off the merged tree rather than incremented from the previous pass's. THE FRAMES WERE RE-CAPTURED at this head rather than re-stamped, and that is what makes the stamps a measurement instead of an argument: the whole `chat-ask-options` set - nine entries, twelve themes, 108 frames - was re-taken with the committed capturer against a real Storybook, twice (once at `9c82dce4f`, and again at `head` once the gate and harness repairs were committed, which is why `dirtyWorkingTree` is FALSE and describes committed source rather than a work in progress), and 0 of those 108 differ from the committed frame in bytes on either run. The re-capture is required here on the repository's own rule, not out of caution: the upstream delta this rebase brought in REACHES the set's import closure, because `src/renderer/src/shared/hooks/use-canonical-session.ts` and `src/shared/desktop-session-contract.ts` are both in the esbuild closure of `canonical/ask-options.stories.tsx`, so the intersection argument the repository's other re-stamps use could not have settled it. This base also moved the contract of the component the set photographs - `CanonicalTranscript` replaced its `error` slot with the published `failure` notice and made `onReconnect` required - and the story that renders it was still passing the old props, so the renderer type check failed on the rebased head until `9c82dce4f` recompiled it against them. That fix passes different props and moves no pixel, which the byte-identical re-capture measures rather than assumes. THE CITATIONS were re-pointed, not carried across, and the three of them are the three a rebase re-spells: `head` and `partialCapture.refreshedAtHead` name this pass, and `partialCapture.addedAtHead` held a pre-rebase spelling this rebase orphaned - resolvable on this machine only through the backup ref the rebase left beside the branch, and therefore nowhere a reviewer can fetch - and now names `bfcc614e9`, its replay in this lineage. That pairing is a `git range-diff` result rather than a positional guess, and the one deviation among the fourteen pairs is named in the `partialCapture` note beside it. Three rebases in a row had left citations of exactly that kind in this file, each found by a reviewer's eye and none by a gate the author runs; `scripts/evidence-manifest.test.mjs` now binds this half too, so the next one fails a test the author already runs. At this head `stampFailures` is 0, `citationFailures` is 0, and each of those three citations is an ancestor of `HEAD` - the ancestry check added here, which is the one that would have caught the last three. Both tree hashes are of the COMMITTED trees, so they name source rather than a work in progress. The rest of this manifest is the merged tree, counted off it rather than added from either side: this branch's own sets, and `main`'s evidence since the branch's base.

countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 1164 at this head, and the assertion is the definition rather than a restatement of it: 1487 `.webp` are committed under `docs/evidence`, 323 of them sit inside the 26 declared sets below, and the remaining 1106 are the sweep's. Re-derived for THIS tree and stated once. The exclusion is by DIRECTORY, which is why the set list below and this number cannot disagree: every declared set's `frames` field matched the frames under its own path when this was written (the check this field's own history needed - `main`'s `composer-readings` used to state 23 against 34 frames and was repaired on `main` in `05a48ca4c`, not here). Two earlier derivations are deleted rather than quoted, on the rule this field already carries: a stale derivation is worse here than none, because the field's whole justification is that a reader can re-compute it, and one that does not resolve teaches them to stop checking. `check-evidence.mjs` fails when these terms disagree with it - in the fast half as well as in the sweep, so the field cannot lag the disk for a whole review round again (code review round 4, m4). This branch carries no version bump of its own: it is rebased onto the release commit rather than merged with a bump, so `package.json` on it reads `0.22.1`, byte-identical to `origin/main`'s apart from the `test:desktop` file list, which is what the repository's version-bump guard reads.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 161 entries, counted off the capturer's own literal by the gate itself rather than summed from the two sides. 152 of them are `main`'s own list at this branch's base, and the nine this branch adds are the `chat-ask-options` entries: eight stories, with `wrapping-labels` counting twice because a story id captured at two widths is written with its width in the path (`wrapping-labels@1024` and `wrapping-labels@560`). 152 + 9 = 161 is a derivation, not the assertion: the gate counts the list and fails a mismatch, so this field cannot silently lag its own source - which is exactly how it read 115 against the capturer's 124 for a whole review round (code review round 3, M1), and why the number is now counted rather than reasoned.
countsMean.themes: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `THEMES.length` - 12. Asserted the same way as `surfaces`: the gate counts the capturer's own list and fails a mismatch.

partialCapture.note: The narrowed runs this branch has taken on top of the last full sweep, which is what `countsMean.frames` is asserted against. FIRST, the ask-options remediation recapture, cited at `bfcc614e9` - this branch's current spelling of that commit. Its earlier spellings went unreachable each time the branch was rebased (onto v0.21.0, twice more during round 4, and again onto v0.22.1), which is the re-pointing repair the manifest's other citations carry: a citation is only evidence if a reader can resolve it. The spelling is `git range-diff`'s over the fourteen replayed commits rather than this note's positional guess, and the pairings are the ones it reports: entry 4 (`2523612b6`, the recapture this run repeated), entries 7, 8, 11, 12 and 14 carry IDENTICAL patches across the rebase, and entry 5 is the single pair whose patch differs - in exactly one file, `scripts/vite-plugins/desktop-proxy.ts`, where that commit's 22 added lines are 15 lines of comment plus the seven-line guard `if (res.headersSent) { res.destroy(); return; }`. Those seven lines are present in this lineage byte-for-byte, landed independently by `main`'s own `8505bb752`, so only the duplicate comment prose is dropped and `main`'s own comment for the same guard stands in its place. Every other file's added and removed line sets are byte-identical between the two spellings, `scripts/click-proof.mjs` (309 added lines) and this set's `harness/ask-gate.vite.mjs` (167) among them, whose blob hashes are equal. It was a `--only=chat-ask-options` run: 122 frames moved, read out of `git diff --name-status 2523612b6 -- docs/evidence` filtered to `.webp` rather than counted by hand - 86 rewritten in place (84 in the swept set and the live pair's 2), 24 added as the two width-suffixed entries above (`wrapping-labels` existed only as the single-width `chat-ask-options/wrapping-labels/` before it, which is design round 1's D5: a story id captured at two widths is written with its width in the path), and 12 stale duplicates deleted rather than left behind, because a second copy of the same story at the same 1024 column would have been stale evidence counted as swept. `check-evidence.mjs` asserts the 120 of those 122 that fall outside the declared sets, which is why `refreshedFrames` exceeds the moved `.webp` count and why the deleted 12 are in it. SECOND, this round's re-verification: the same `--only=chat-ask-options` run at `refreshedAtHead`, the narrowed run's full nine entries across all twelve themes, 108 frames - re-taken to check that the frames are still pictures of this head's `src` rather than to re-argue it, and every one of the 108 came back byte-identical to the committed frame on disk (`git status docs/evidence` after the run names this manifest and nothing else). It ran twice, at `refreshedFromHead` and again at `refreshedAtHead`, the second time once the gate and harness repairs were committed so that `dirtyWorkingTree` would describe committed source; `refreshedFrames` is 216 rather than 108 because the capturer accumulates across the runs of one pass while the head stays inside that pass's ancestry - the count is frames taken, and 216 were taken, the second 108 of them moving no bytes. It is recorded because it is what licenses the tree stamps above. `frames` and `surfaces` are re-derived from the tree and from the capturer's own list as they stand rather than incremented from the previous values, which is what the capture script's own `+ addedSurfaces.length` would have got wrong here (the two new entries share one story ID, so the entry count moved by one and the directory count by two) and wrong again on this rebase, where upstream's list grew under this branch: 152 of the 161 swept entries are `main`'s own. One more narrowed run is recorded here because this file is the manifest's only per-run record and this round would otherwise have erased it: `main`'s tool-row round (`--only=chat-tool-rows`, refreshed 26 frames across 12 stories, 0 added, at `59997deb1`), which is where `chat-tool-rows/*` and the `tool-rows-4px-rejected` set come from. `previousRefresh` above is the model-picker remediation's two runs, unchanged, because they are still true of frames on disk. `refreshedStories` names this branch's own entries and nothing else. It carried nine `canvas-workspace--*` ids when this block's citation fields still described `main`'s pass; the branch's own pass replaced those fields, and a story list for a pass the block no longer cites is a record of something else, so it is deleted rather than left to disagree with the citation beside it. `main`'s own manifest still records that pass, which is where a reader following those ids should look.

previousRefresh.note: The capture that ADDED this branch's twelve picker/band surfaces. Recorded here because the remediation round's own narrowed capture overwrites `addedFrames`/`addedSurfaces` in place, and an addition that disappears from the manifest reads as though the stories had always been swept.

supplementary.source: the REAL built Electron app - pnpm build, then electron . from this tree's own out/ with LOCAL_OPERATOR_UI_WINDOW_MODE=headless, its own --user-data-dir and its own CDP port - against an ISOLATED `local-operator serve` on a scratch LOCAL_OPERATOR_CONFIG_DIR/HOME and a scratch cwd, paired through a shared LOCAL_OPERATOR_DESKTOP_TOKEN; driven over raw CDP by out/evidence-harness/drive-mentioned-files.mjs, with the session seeded by out/evidence-harness/seed-mentioned-files.mjs and every path it mentions generated by out/evidence-harness/make-fixtures.mjs (the two-second H.264 clip the video frame needs is the one fixture that shells out to ffmpeg, and the run refuses rather than substituting a still or the viewer's error state). The harness is gitignored under out/, like the chat-title and sidebar-new-chat ones. All four frames are cropped to the canvas panel's own measured rect, so none carries the sidebar, the session list or the transcript; the un-cropped window frames are written beside them and left uncommitted. One harness accommodation is recorded in this set's README and is visible in the frames: the renderer's CSP names the :1111 hosts for `media-src` as well, so the harness widens that single directive in the BUILD OUTPUT (out/ is gitignored, src/renderer/ is untouched) or the video viewer cannot load at all from the isolated backend.
supplementary.why: The claims under review are claims about a running app that no sweep can photograph. The panel frame shows the producer firing over a real transcript: six inferred paths become six tiles under the head, with the ghost carrying the `No longer on disk` receipt and the video tile painting a real frame. The PDF frame is the only one that exercises the real read path - main-process readFileBytes over IPC on real bytes, into Chromium's own viewer over a blob URL with `#toolbar=0`. The two video frames are the only committed pictures of that viewer's WORKING state, which design review round 1 asked for by name and which cannot come from Storybook: the story's stub cannot answer the backend's Range route, so the swept video frames are the error state by declaration. They are captured in both brand palettes because the platform player's own chrome sits on `sunken` and that pairing is the one the design round measured as marginal in the light palettes (D7).
supplementary.capturedAtHeadNote: Re-driven at the head the branch stood on before an earlier rebase (`8fc94e602`, orphaned by that force-push), and cited as that commit's replay in this history, because the re-drive is what the citation has to rest on and a replay is the only spelling of it this history carries. The chain is `8fc94e602` -> `71cd00ae0` (the rebase onto 0.19.7) -> `72225e78f` (this rebase), each a replay of the one before it. The re-drive was exact: the app was RE-BUILT from that tree (`pnpm build` with `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL` pointing at the scratch backend, which the run verifies the built renderer carries) and driven through the same isolated harness twice, and a fresh encode of each new PNG along the same lossy path (`magick -quality 88`, the setting the swept frames use) hashed to the committed git blob - `d6498ce493` (files-panel/dark), `b016a285d2` (pdf-viewer/light), `bbd1c35bec` (video-viewer/dark), `c2e8c5e987` (video-viewer/light) - so nothing was rewritten and the pixels on disk are that pass's own output, not an earlier pass's carried forward. Every reading the driver takes was unchanged: the same six mentioned paths in the same order with `march-export.csv` carrying `No longer on disk`, six tiles under the panel head, the PDF inside Chromium's viewer on a `blob:` URL titled `PDF: invoice-review.pdf` with the open-in-OS control and zero CSP violations, and the video `readyState 4 / currentTime 1.2 / duration 2 / 480x270 / error null` on the media route (the driver refuses to write a video frame unless the clip decodes). The crop was unchanged too: the panel's own measured rect, 1598x1932+1858+0 at a 1728x966 CSS viewport, dpr 2. Neither this rebase nor the one before it re-drove the set, and the reason is in this set's `source`: the frames are cropped to the canvas panel, so the sidebar this rebase's delta touches is not in them at all, and the frame-to-source question is settled by the byte-identical re-drive rather than by re-running it. One harness note for the next pass, recorded because the fix belongs to the gitignored harness rather than to this set: the driver's process is held alive by its spawned Electron child after it has written its report, so the runner stalls between the two theme passes; ending only that child (the PID the run started, never a process found by name) lets the pass continue. That chain's last spelling (`72225e78f085abbe46a556a4ce1409791616f021`) went unreachable in turn when #128 was squash-merged and the branch deleted, so the citation is now its reachable spelling on `main`, `e8ebe5c6d189ed07dc69515e351d9576b35a8d6d`, whose `docs/evidence/mentioned-files-app` tree is byte-identical to `main`'s - the set this entry declares.

supplementary.source: the REAL built Electron app (`pnpm build`, then `docs/evidence/window-mode/harness/run.sh` with EXTRA_SEED=seed-model-picker.mjs and DRIVE_SCRIPT=drive-model-picker.mjs, headless, 1380x900) against an isolated `local-operator serve` on a port the script owns, 0 frontmost samples in every run and 0 renderer errors. Sixteen states, and they come from TWO runs because two starting states are needed: fifteen from the branch's own seed (no provider credential, i.e. the refusal path — the seed the `before-*` halves were taken under, so the pairs still differ by the change and not by the setup), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames from a second run on QA's credentialed seed (`/tmp/qa130/seed-qa.mjs`, a synthetic `openai` credential written through the backend's own AuthStore) — without a credential the owner refuses every switch, so a switch it ACCEPTS does not exist there. The second run's frames are prefixed `cred-` by the driver so no frame can be mistaken for the other seed's. `localOperatorDark` is the app's own default theme, which is the only theme the harness boots into. **U7 round.** The one frame UX U7 invalidated was re-captured on the fixed head and one `before-*` half was added beside it: `needs-sign-in-pick-settled` now shows `This session runs anthropic/claude-opus-5.` (the row the check is on) where the pre-fix frame showed `openai/gpt-4.1`, and that pre-fix frame is committed as `before-header-names-the-switch` — the only `before-*` half taken on this branch's own pre-fix head (`ccbeb0e2a`) rather than on the merge-base, because UX filed U7 against the branch rather than against the base. That run is also the first whose cache lives inside the scratch root: `run.sh` now sets `HOME="$SCRATCH/home"` (QA round 2, Q3 — the catalogue cache resolves from `HOME`, not from the config dir), so the seed copies the same `*.listing.json` files the earlier run read into the scratch home, and nothing outside `/tmp` is written. Both runs' measurements are committed beside the frames (`picker-metrics.json`, `picker-metrics-credentialed.json`), so every number the README quotes is re-derivable from the tree.
supplementary.why: the claim is that a hover, a keyboard highlight, an in-flight pick and the OUTCOME of that pick are perceivable — properties of computed style and of timing that no palette assertion and no component test can see. The unit suite asserts the classes, the transitions and the reading rule (`scripts/picker-feedback.test.mjs`); only a frame of the running app shows the ground and the edge the row actually paints inside a dialog whose own ground is `elevated`, and what the user is left with when the answer arrives after the dialog is gone. The `before-*` halves carry the defect as a measurement: the active row's computed background is `rgb(40,35,24)`, identical to the dialog's, and `before-pointer-left-list` is byte-identical to `before-keyboard-highlight` (AE 0 of 4,813,440 px). Seven of the sixteen states are after-only, and that is the finding rather than an omission: each is a state the old code could not produce or could not report — the pointer's structural edge in a palette where the wash collapses (D12), the footer naming the row Enter acts on while that row is off screen (U1), the band holding a labelled spinner while the pick is unconfirmed (U3), the refusal landing with the dialog already closed (U2), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames (Q1). The transcript note count is measured either side of the U2 case — 1 before the click, 2 after it, with the dialog closed 80 ms in — because the refusal sentence is identical for every refused pick and only a count can prove a second one was written. The U7 pair is measured rather than described: between the two frames AE is 85,307 px (1.77%) of 4,813,440, of which 13,230 px (2% fuzz) sit in one 952x64 band across the header sentence's own text line and 274 px are the clock.

WHAT THE PAIR PROVES, and this replaces the correction the QA round asked for: after-click/localOperatorDark.webp IS a picture of the gate resolving. The driver pressed and released at the option's hit-tested centre (x 960, y 587, elementFromPoint resolving to the option itself, `aim.hitTested`), the card is GONE rather than the page failing, and focus is on the composer. click-result.json carries `resolved: true` and `after: {"found": false, "count": 0}` against `before: {"found": true, "count": 3}`. The previous pair's after frame showed three failure surfaces instead of a cleared card (the Vite dev server had died mid-run from ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT in desktop-proxy.ts), which is fixed, so the frame is back at `after-click/` - a name that now tells the truth about what it shows.

The click ITSELF is recorded, not merely photographed: click-result.json carries the pre-click DOM, the aim point, and the post-click DOM. owner-answer.json is the owner's own return value, {"PAIRING": ["Popup is open - generate the pairing code"]} - the option's LABEL, never an index. The record's field names are the driver's own as of this regeneration (`textContent`, `accessibleName`, `pointerEvents`, with the aria-hidden ordinal stripped from `accessibleName`), so the record and the driver now agree; the earlier disclosure that the record called that field `names` is removed because the mismatch it documented is gone (code review round 2, n7 and F4).

WHAT UNBLOCKED IT, since the previous entry said the healthy re-capture was deferred as impossible: the harness seeded the provoking user turn AFTER `/rig-arm`, i.e. after `watching_surfaces()` went non-empty and therefore after the app had already been answered its history request. The durable row never reached the transcript, CanonicalTranscript collapsed to h-0 as designed, and the driver failed with `no fieldset` - which read as 'the driver cannot aim' but was a fixture armed one page-load too late. The turn is now appended before the SERVER ANNOUNCES ITSELF, so the history request sees it and the gate follows it, which is how the app always reaches this state. That is a harness fix, not a product change; QA round 2's Q1 is closed by running the committed rig rather than by re-labelling the gap.
Captured in localOperatorDark only: this is a wire-and-interaction proof, not a palette proof. The twelve-theme question is answered by chat-ask-options/, which the sweep takes across every palette.
